scene: At a low home play table, Dad sits screen-left and Child kneels screen-right. Child is the four-year-old tiger boy in his unchanged yellow T-shirt. A toy train track forms a nearly complete ring on the table, with one clearly visible gap where the final curve piece is missing; that loose curve piece rests beside the gap, and one small train is parked on the track nearby. This track set is the only essential prop group. Locked 16:9 medium two-shot shows both faces, hands, the gap and the train. Keep the single gap and the loose curve piece stable until they click together; no extra toys, tools or people. Dad steadies the track but never connects the piece for Child.

emotion.baseline: Calm, warm and regulated baseline at ordinary family conversation volume. Dad is available and matter-of-fact; Child is focused on finishing his track ring.
emotion.allowed_shift: The failed join brings only a brief puzzled look. Child asks for help at normal volume and shows quiet satisfaction when his own push makes the ring close.
emotion.forbidden: No frustrated shouting, whining spectacle, angry faces, arm flinging, pounding the track or exaggerated victory gestures. Dad does not scold, take over, withhold help or turn the repair into a test. Keep face and body proportions stable.

clips.start: The nearly complete track ring lies on the table with one gap; the loose curve piece rests beside the gap and the train waits on the track; Dad and Child have empty hands.
clips.action: Dad glances along the track ring during his opening line. Child tries to press the curve piece into the gap once with both hands, feels it not click, and asks for help at normal volume. Dad leans in slightly and asks which piece is the trouble.
clips.end: The curve piece still rests unconnected beside the gap; the train waits on the track; Child's hands rest beside the curve and Dad looks at the gap.

clips.start: The curve piece still rests unconnected beside the gap; the train waits on the track; Child's hands rest beside the curve and Dad looks at the gap.
clips.action: Child taps the curve piece lightly while naming it and the ends that will not click. Dad places one steady hand on the track beside the gap during his plan. Only after that support is in place, Child grips the curve piece with both hands and pushes it into the gap until the ends visibly click together. The ring closes before Child reports it.
clips.end: The track ring is complete with no gap; Child has empty hands above the closed join and Dad's hand still rests on the track beside it; the train waits on the ring.

clips.start: The track ring is complete with no gap; Child has empty hands above the closed join and Dad's hand still rests on the track beside it; the train waits on the ring.
clips.action: Dad releases the track and gestures toward the waiting train. Child picks up the train with his right hand and pushes it slowly along the ring across the closed join, watching it pass. He looks up at Dad with a small pleased smile during his thanks.
clips.end: Child holds the train on the completed ring just past the closed join; Dad has empty hands and smiles warmly; the track ring lies fully connected on the table.
